label: prop:knot-operator-transition
title: Nucleon-addition operators: Hopf link at $A{=}3$, trefoil at $A{=}4$
html:
The operator that adds the (A{+}1)-th nucleon to a nucleus of mass number A has a definite knot type:

Transition Operator Dominant NF Knot type
p \to D \sigma_0 - h/2 \sigma_0 single crossing
D \to {}^3\!H \sigma_1^{-1}(\sigma_0{-}h/2) L_- Hopf link
D \to {}^3\!\mathrm{He} (\sigma_1{-}h/2)\sigma_0 L_- Hopf link
{}^3\!H \to {}^4\!\mathrm{He} (\sigma_0{-}h/2)(\sigma_1{-}h/2)\sigma_0 e^- trefoil
{}^3\!\mathrm{He} \to {}^4\!\mathrm{He} (\sigma_0{-}h/2)\sigma_1^{-1}(\sigma_0{-}h/2) e^- trefoil

The p-n factors are written \sigma - h/2, the \delta = 0 convention; the canonical colour-tube-weighted form is \sigma - h(1/2 - \delta/4), with \delta the substrate flavour split of prop:flavor-split-substrate. The Dominant NF and Knot type columns are unaffected. Recomputing the H_3 normal form of all five operators under both conventions returns the same dominant basis element in every case, with dominance margins of 4.7\times to 9.6\times against a relative perturbation of only \delta/2 \approx 6.9 \times 10^{-4} on the p-n shift — four orders of magnitude of headroom (knot_operator_transition_convention_robustness_probe.py, 8 assertions). The convention is recorded because the operators are written in it, not because the conclusion depends on it.

The knot hierarchy progresses from unknot (1 nucleon) to single crossing (2) to Hopf link (3) to trefoil (4). The 4th nucleon completes the trefoil topology, explaining why {}^4\!\mathrm{He} has the strongest binding per nucleon among light nuclei. \square
